content: {"id":"01a0f88a-b2bf-7310-ac87-960b6c675259","created":true,"summary":"Tax uses ROUND_HALF_UP (finance reversal, Oct 2026)"}

I updated `tax_for` in `src/billing/tax.py` so tax now rounds half-up, as finance asked.

**About the existing code:** `tax_for` didn't have any rounding to change. It just raised `NotImplementedError`, so I wrote the function. It multiplies the cents amount by the rate as a `Decimal`, rounds to whole cents with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, and returns an integer. The repo has no tests for it. I ran a quick manual check: 250¢ at 5% gives 13 and 350¢ at 5% gives 18, so halves round up.

**Memory conflict:** the project memory still said tax uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) and explicitly said not to use half-up, based on the March 2026 decision with finance. Your instruction is newer, so I followed it. I saved a new decision memory recording the switch to half-up on 2026-10-01 and marked the old one as superseded, so future sessions won't revert it.

I haven't committed anything.
